discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (moire quantum materials)

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

nominees.name: Rafi Bistritzer
nominees.affiliation: Applied Materials, Israel (formerly University of Texas at Austin)

subfield: Condensed matter physics: two-dimensional and correlated electron systems
motivation: In 2011 Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted that two graphene sheets twisted by about 1.1 degrees develop nearly flat electronic bands. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group fabricated such devices with a controlled twist and found gate-tunable correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity, all in one clean two-dimensional device made only of carbon. The twist angle has since become a new tuning parameter for quantum matter. It opened the field of moire materials, which has produced orbital magnetism, the quantum anomalous Hall effect, Chern insulators and, most recently, the zero-field fractional quantum anomalous Hall effect in twisted semiconductors and graphene. The experiments are simple in concept: stacking, gating and low-temperature transport. Yet they give clear quantised and correlated signatures. This close interplay of theory and device ingenuity has made the moire platform for strongly correlated and topological physics one of the most fertile in condensed matter.
